actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: KinDER is a physical reasoning benchmark for robot learning and planning
The package declares mujoco~=3.3.0 as a dependency
The RBY1A model is the MJCF model rby1, compiled in radians with autolimits and eulerseq xyz
The model sets no option timestep: its two <option> elements name only the implicitfast integrator and the elliptic cone; the only timestep text is a commented-out line
The root default class gives every motor the control range -3000000 to 3000000 and ctrllimited true
The model declares 24 motors: two wheel, six torso, seven left arm, seven right arm and two head motors, all without a local ctrlrange so the root default applies
The model has one free root joint (world_j) and 28 hinge or slide joints: the two wheels, six torso joints, seven joints per arm, two fingers per gripper and two head joints
The joint limits are stated per joint; examples are torso_0 -0.349066 to 0.349066 rad, torso_1 -1.0472 to 1.52173 rad and right_arm_4 -6.28319 to 6.28319 rad
The two fingers of a gripper are coupled by an equality constraint
The dynamic3d RBY1A robot environment inserts rby1a_model_v1.2.xml into the task scene XML
The dynamic3d env selects RBY1ARobotEnv when the task's robot type is rby1a
The base MuJoCo environment defines SIMULATION_TIMESTEP as 0.0005 s
The base MuJoCo environment writes its SIMULATION_TIMESTEP into the XML option element before loading the model

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates one model deterministically from one state; the bridge records a seed but a reset restores the model defaults and no seed selects a different initial state.  The package's fake is deterministic too, but its placeholder dynamics are not the model's.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not the MuJoCo engine: it parses the model file for the joint and actuator counts and the control ranges, then advances a placeholder first-order motion; it computes no equations of motion, inertias, contacts, equality constraints or actuator dynamics, so its trajectories are not valid simulation results

the model file states no <option timestep>; timestep_ms 2.0 is the fake's placeholder for MuJoCo's library default, while the upstream dynamic3d environment sets 0.0005 s when it composes a scene (mujoco_utils.py:27,774-781), so the real step of a served model is not verified here
the driver serves the RBY1A model file, not the Gymnasium task environment: the task config, objects, observations, rewards, goals and episode limits of the dynamic3d envs are not modelled

the mesh assets referenced through the model's include files are read from the clone by a real MuJoCo load but are not resolved by the fake; no rendering and no sensor, camera or contact model is served
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model step only
the model was never loaded by the MuJoCo engine where the gate ran and was never compared with a real RBY1A robot; nothing ran on hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
